subject: orange river
title: What If a River Turned Orange Overnight? Colorado's Did in 2015

scenes.text: What if a river turned orange overnight? Colorado's did, and the spill wasn't the real problem.
August 5, 2015. A crew at the old Gold King Mine accidentally sets loose 3 million gallons of wastewater.
It carries about 880,000 pounds of metals. Early tests find lead in the river at 3,500 times the normal level.
The stained water runs more than 100 miles, into New Mexico. Towns and farmers stop drawing from the river.
Within about a week the colour is gone and the water tests as it did before. No fish kills reported.
Then the EPA did the sums: the spill held about as much metal as the mine leaks anyway every four to seven days. In 2016, 48 mine sites there joined the Superfund list.

description:
What if a river turned orange overnight? On 5 August 2015 a crew working for the EPA at the Gold King Mine near Silverton, Colorado, accidentally released 3 million gallons of mine wastewater into the Animas River, carrying about 880,000 pounds of metals.
The plume was visible for more than 100 miles; by 13 August samples were back to pre-spill conditions and no fish kills were reported. The EPA later put the metals at about four to seven days of the mine's ordinary drainage, and 48 nearby mine sites were added to the Superfund list in 2016.

first_comment: The first estimate was 1 million gallons; a stream gauge showed it was three times that. What would you do if your river changed colour?
